content: 1. Darunavir and sufentanil: Darunavir increases the plasma levels and effects of sufentanil by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction may lead to enhanced or prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Cobicistat and sufentanil: Cobicistat also increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Darunavir and sunitinib: Darunavir increases sunitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 4. Cobicistat and sunitinib: Cobicistat similarly increases sunitinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Darunavir and suvorexant: Darunavir increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Cobicistat and suvorexant: Cobicistat also increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Darunavir and tacrolimus: Darunavir increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 8. Cobicistat and tacrolimus: Cobicistat increases tacrolimus levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 9. Darunavir and tadalafil: Darunavir increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), start tadalafil at 20 mg/day and increase to 40 mg/day if tolerated. For erectile dysfunction (ED), limit to a single dose of 10 mg every 72 hours. 10. Cobicistat and tadalafil: Cobicistat increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat and talazoparib: Cobicistat increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting the breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions. 12. Cobicistat and tamoxifen: Cobicistat decreases tamoxifen efficacy by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Darunavir and tamsulosin: Darunavir increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat and tamsulosin: Cobicistat also increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Darunavir and tasimelteon: Darunavir increases tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Tazemetostat and darunavir: Tazemetostat decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat and tazemetostat: Cobicistat increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Tecovirimat and darunavir: Tecovirimat decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Darunavir and temsirolimus: Darunavir increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 20. Cobicistat and temsirolimus: Cobicistat increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 21. Darunavir and teniposide: Darunavir increases teniposide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be used. 22. Cobicistat and teniposide: Cobicistat increases teniposide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Darunavir and terbinafine: Darunavir increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Cobicistat and terbinafine: Cobicistat also increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir and tezacaftor: Darunavir increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Cobicistat and tezacaftor: Cobicistat increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 27. Darunavir and theophylline: Darunavir increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cobicistat and theophylline: Cobicistat also increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cobicistat and thioridazine: Cobicistat increases thioridazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Darunavir and tiagabine: Darunavir increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cobicistat and tiagabine: Cobicistat also increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Darunavir and ticagrelor: Darunavir increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat and ticagrelor: Cobicistat also increases ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Darunavir and timolol: Darunavir increases timolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Darunavir and tinidazole: Darunavir increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cobicistat and tinidazole: Cobicistat also increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Darunavir and tipranavir: Darunavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 38. Cobicistat and tipranavir: Cobicistat increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. 39. Darunavir and tivozanib: Darunavir increases tivozanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Cobicistat and tramadol: Cobicistat increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 41. Darunavir and tramadol: Darunavir also increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 42. Cobicistat and trazodone: Cobicistat increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Darunavir and trazodone: Darunavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Darunavir and triamcinolone acetonide: Darunavir increases triamcinolone acetonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Cobicistat and triamcinolone acetonide: Cobicistat also increases triamcinolone acetonide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Darunavir and triazolam: Darunavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of severe sedation or respiratory depression. 47. Cobicistat and triazolam: Cobicistat also increases triazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. 48. Darunavir and trimipramine: Darunavir increases trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat and trimipramine: Cobicistat also increases trimipramine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely.
